tool.name: Derive amplicon panel
tool.description: reconstruct an amplicon panel FASTA from genome-mapped reads (coverage peaks = amplicons), PyEuk derive-panel
tool.command: ## Amplicon locations are a property of the assay, shared by every specimen, so this is a ## COHORT-level reduction over a SAMPLE of genome-mapped BAMs -- not a per-specimen step. mkdir -p bams && #for $i, $b in enumerate($bams) ln -s '$b' 'bams/${i}.bam' && ln -s '${b.metadata.bam_index}' 'bams/${i}.bam.bai' && #end for ln -s '$genome' genome.fa && pyeuk derive-panel --bams bams/*.bam --genome genome.fa --sample $advanced.sample --min-depth-frac $advanced.min_depth_frac --min-abs-depth $advanced.min_abs_depth --min-length $advanced.min_length --merge-gap $advanced.merge_gap --pad $advanced.pad --prefix '$advanced.prefix' --out '$panel' --out-bed '$bed' --out-qc '$qc'

param.name: bams
param.label: Genome-mapped BAMs (a sample of the cohort)
param.help: Reads mapped to the reference GENOME (not a panel). A representative subset is enough; use the Advanced 'How many BAMs to scan' to cap it.

param.name: genome
param.label: Reference genome the BAMs were mapped to
param.help: Used to extract each peak's sequence into the panel.

param.name: sample
param.label: How many BAMs to scan
param.help: Evenly strided across the input. 0 = all.

param.name: min_depth_frac
param.label: Minimum peak depth (fraction of max)
param.help: A peak must reach this fraction of the run's MAX coverage. Data-adaptive: amplicon peaks sit far above background, so this needs no retuning across datasets.

param.name: merge_gap
param.label: Merge peaks closer than (bp)
param.help: Joins a peak that dips in the middle.

param.name: pad
param.label: Pad each peak by (bp)
param.help: Extend both ends to catch primer flanks.

tool.help:
**Derive an amplicon panel from the data**
Targeted-amplicon reads do not spread over the genome -- they pile up on the amplified regions as sharp, contiguous coverage peaks against an empty background. Map the reads to the reference **genome**, and each peak is an amplicon; its genome sequence is the panel entry. That is how a curated panel is built in the first place.
Use this when you do **not** have the panel for a cohort. The output FASTA is a drop-in for the *panel* input of the standard read-level haplotype-typing workflow: derive the panel here, then feed it there.
The peak threshold is **data-adaptive** -- a fraction of the run's own maximum depth -- so it does not need retuning across datasets or sequencing depths.
